results.title: Cops nab employee for violating NIRC
results.description: BUTUAN CITY – A 26-year-old employee was arrested in Gen. Luna, Siargao Island, Surigao del Norte for an alleged tax violation. In a report to Police Regional Office-13 Director Police Brig. Gen. Rolindo M. Suguilon on Friday, Sept. 18, Surigao del Norte Police Provincial Office (PPO) Director Police Col. Warren E. Dablo said the suspect was arrested by the Gen. Luna Municipal Police Station at 9:15 a.m. on Wednesday, Sept. 16, for allegedly violating Section 255 of the National Internal Revenue Code (NIRC) which covers the willful failure to file returns, pay taxes, maintain accurate records, or remit withheld taxes as required by law. The suspect’s warrant was issued by the Regional Trial Court, Tenth Judicial Region, Branch 31, Dapa, Surigao del Norte on Feb. 13, 2026. Dablo added that the suspect is under the custody of the Gen. Luna MPS for documentation and proper disposition. “Surigao del Norte PPO and all municipal police units will continue to locate and apprehend wanted persons, through solid intelligence and proper coordination that fully upholds the law and respects due process,” Dablo added. Suguilon ordered all regional, provincial, and city mobile force commanders as well as provincial and city directors and municipal chiefs of police to maximize their intelligence-driven operations for the arrest of other fugitives.

results.title: Getting connectivity is not the end of the developer’s responsibility; GERC Explains Why
results.description: Getting grid connectivity does not by itself insulate a renewable energy developer from responsibility for completing the remaining transmission and evacuation infrastructure within the stipulated timeline, the Gujarat Electricity Regulatory Commission (GERC) has held in a recent order involving Rolex Rings Ltd. The commission rejected Rolex Rings’ plea for an extension of time for its 9 MW captive solar project in Gujarat, finding that the circumstances cited by the company did not constitute unforeseen or uncontrollable events that materially prevented it from completing the required evacuation infrastructure. The order, provides a detailed view of how GERC is likely to assess force majeure claims arising from delays after connectivity has already been granted. Connectivity comes with a project-execution obligation Rolex Rings is developing a 9 MW solar PV project for captive use in Gujarat. Gujarat Energy Transmission Corporation Ltd (GETCO) granted Stage-I and Stage-II connectivity to the project on May 31, 2024, for evacuation to the 220 kV Sadla substation. Under the applicable tariff framework, developers of solar projects between 1 MW and 100 MW are required to furnish a bank guarantee and complete the allocated evacuation infrastructure, including the transmission line, bays and metering system, within 1.5 years from the allotment of transmission capacity. For Rolex Rings, the deadline worked out to November 30, 2025. The company subsequently sought an extension, citing several circumstances that it said had affected its ability to meet the deadline. These included difficulties in finalising the sharing arrangement for common evacuation infrastructure with Madhura Industrial Textiles, delays in obtaining approvals under Sections 68 and 164 of the Electricity Act, 2003, and heavy rainfall during the 2025 monsoon. GERC, however, said the company had not established the necessary causal link between these events and its inability to complete the evacuation infrastructure within the prescribed period. Sharing arrangement was not force majeure A significant part of the dispute concerned the common evacuation infrastructure that Rolex Rings was required to share with another generator. Rolex Rings argued that uncertainty over the lead generator and delays in coordination with Madhura Industrial Textiles affected the finalisation of the evacuation scheme and consequently delayed subsequent approvals and construction. GERC did not accept this as an event beyond the developer's reasonable control. The commission noted that both Rolex Rings and Madhura had received connectivity under the same sharing mechanism on May 31, 2024. It further pointed out that Madhura subsequently completed its evacuation infrastructure and obtained charging permission, demonstrating that the sharing mechanism itself was not an insurmountable impediment to project execution. The commission also noted that the Format-6 agreement governing the sharing arrangement was already part of the approved Detailed Procedure and was therefore known to the parties. According to GERC, the two private generators were required to arrive at the necessary commercial understanding and documentation within the prescribed timeline. A delay in concluding such inter-se commercial arrangements could not be treated as a force majeure event. Developer’s own timeline matters The order also puts considerable emphasis on the sequence in which Rolex Rings took various project-execution steps. The company had argued that it could not finalise the evacuation scheme or proceed with the statutory approval process until the kick-off meeting with GETCO had taken place. GERC, however, found an inconsistency in this position. The commission noted that Rolex Rings had already approached the state government for the required statutory approvals on April 30, 2025, while the kick-off meeting took place later. It also noted that Rolex Rings and Madhura had executed a Lead Generator Agreement before that meeting. The commission therefore concluded that finalisation of the evacuation scheme was not necessarily dependent on the kick-off meeting. This became important in determining whether the subsequent delays could legitimately be attributed to circumstances outside Rolex Rings’ control.
